analysis:
Examined all supplied source, patches and file metadata against the canonical index and selected T-041 detail. ProviderLoop.swift adds an internal loadWeightHasher defaulting to the existing cryptographic hasher (head patch lines 444–445) and an optional verified-hash persistence destination (684–688). ProviderLoop+Testing.swift:143–151 exposes internal setters for these properties; no remote dispatch or attacker-accessible invocation is shown, so their presence does not establish a hash-verification bypass. Integration must examine captureWeightHash, VerifiedWeightHashStore and startup registration consumers to verify persisted hashes remain bound to current loaded bytes and cannot become stale routing or SSD-cache evidence (T-012, T-027, T-041). The declarations alone do not establish that contract.
ProviderLoop+Trust.swift:129 adds GLM5NextWiredLimitNotice.report before existing load-error persistence. Its implementation is absent: check its output, input handling and execution cost, especially whether it preserves the documented no-automatic-log-upload behavior at lines 3–5 and does not expose request-derived data (A-001, TB-003). Existing trust-status diagnostics and connection clearing remain unchanged at head lines 135–157; no new serving grant or authorization bypass is visible (T-052, T-053, T-058). No changes to encryption, billing, attestation verification or privileged fan controls are shown. No concrete regression is supported in this batch; the new persistence consumers and diagnostic callee require cross-file integration review.
